core.edit.mfwWaitTimeTip: When MAS has just launched the game, the first task waits before starting; MaaFW initialisation runs in parallel. Desktop games: MAS waits for the window to appear and then for the screen to settle, each for at most this long, and starts early once the screen settles; no wait if the game window is already open. Emulators: after cold-starting the game along with the emulator, MAS waits at most this long, and starts early once the screen shows content and the game has stopped reading from disk, and keeps waiting if the screen is still black at that point; no wait if the game process is already running, in the foreground or not. Freshly started games are usually still loading, and posting tasks too early makes the script report a recognition failure or a stuck game.

core.setting.display.intro: When every real display output goes away, Windows keeps a placeholder phantom screen: it still reports a normal-looking resolution, but nothing is actually driving it, so game rendering and screen capture may both be unreliable. A cold boot with no output is worse still: Windows comes up at a very small resolution, the game window shrinks, and the game remembers that size. Once enabled, MAS keeps watching the desktop: it attaches a virtual display whenever there is no real display output at all. When a real monitor comes back it is removed right away if nothing is running; while a run is in progress it stays — removing it moves windows onto the returning monitor and breaks PC game runs — and MAS instead asks you with a prompt in the bottom-right corner of the returning monitor, then removes it automatically once the run finishes. {driverLink}; MAS does not ship it.
